name: Spider-Man
funFact: Peter Parker was the first teenage superhero who wasn't just a sidekick.

name: Batman
funFact: Batman has no superpowers — he relies entirely on intellect, martial arts, and technology.

name: Wonder Woman
funFact: Wonder Woman was created by William Moulton Marston, who also invented the lie detector.

name: Iron Man
funFact: Tony Stark was originally created as a challenge — to make readers like an arms dealer.

name: Superman
funFact: Superman is considered the first superhero of the modern comic book era.

name: Black Panther
funFact: Black Panther was the first Black superhero in mainstream American comics.

name: The Flash
funFact: Barry Allen's version of The Flash kickstarted the Silver Age of comics.

name: Captain America
funFact: Captain America's first comic showed him punching Adolf Hitler — a year before the US entered WWII.

name: Thor
funFact: Thor is based on the actual Norse god of thunder from Viking mythology.

name: Green Lantern
funFact: The Green Lantern ring is considered the most powerful weapon in the DC universe.

name: Wolverine
funFact: Wolverine was originally created as a one-off character to fight the Hulk.

name: Aquaman
funFact: Aquaman can communicate telepathically with all marine life, not just fish.

name: Doctor Strange
funFact: Doctor Strange was inspired by Chandu the Magician, a 1930s radio and film character.

name: Cyborg
funFact: Cyborg was the first Black character to be a founding member of the Teen Titans.

name: Hulk
funFact: The Hulk was originally grey in his first issue — the green color was due to a printing error that stuck.

name: Hawkman
funFact: Hawkman has one of the most complicated continuities in DC — he has been rebooted more times than any other hero.

name: Black Widow
funFact: Black Widow started as a villain before becoming one of Marvel's most iconic heroes.

name: Green Arrow
funFact: Green Arrow was originally inspired by Robin Hood and created as a Batman-like archer.

name: Scarlet Witch
funFact: Scarlet Witch once rewrote all of reality with just three words: 'No more mutants.'

name: Shazam
funFact: Shazam (originally Captain Marvel) outsold Superman in the 1940s, making him DC's most popular hero of that era.
